_comment: Every external endpoint used by the MARSWALK data pipeline.
Each entry was opened and verified on 2026-11-13; 'verified' records what
the probe actually returned. Nothing in this file is a guessed URL.
provenance: REAL = downloaded from NASA/USGS; DERIVED = computed by us from
REAL data; MODELED = built from published measurements, not a raw dataset.
AOI = footprint of the HiRISE DTM that covers Curiosity's traverse from
the Glen Torridon clay-bearing unit (sol ~1167) through Gediz Vallis to
the sulfate-bearing unit and the 2025 boxwork campaign (sol 5070).
This is NOT the 5.4S/137.8E point in the original brief: no HiRISE DTM
covers that point, and Curiosity has never been there. See README.

dem.title: MRO HiRISE Digital Terrain Model, Gale Crater filled channel and fan deposit
dem.access: HTTP range requests (server sends Accept-Ranges: bytes), so only the AOI rows are downloaded, not the full ~540 MB file
dem.verified: 2026-11-13: HEAD 200, Accept-Ranges bytes; label parsed; sample row returned continuous float elevations

ortho.title: MRO HiRISE, Curiosity Roving Site Mosaic
ortho.tile_scheme: geographic, top-left (-180, 90), matrix 2^(z+1) x 2^z, 256 px tiles
ortho.verified: 2026-11-13: WMTSCapabilities parsed; tiles return 8-bit greyscale PNG

traverse.title: Curiosity actual driven path
traverse.fields: RMC, site, drive, sol, easting, northing, elev_geoid, lon, lat, roll, pitch, yaw, tilt

pov_images.title: Curiosity raw image archive
pov_images.selection: Navcam/Mastcam frames near each station's pinned sol, scored for whether they look out across the ground. Raw Navcam EDRs render sky DARK, not bright, so the test is a dark band at the top plus textured ground at the bottom; that also rejects the sky-only calibration frames in the archive. Frames that fail are kept but labelled 'workspace' rather than implying a panorama.

geology.title: Global Geologic Map of Mars (USGS SIM 3292)
geology.source: USGS Astrogeology, served via NASA Mars Trek
geology.status: NOT shipped as a map layer
geology.reason: This is the only geologic map in the Trek catalogue that covers the AOI, and it is global at 1:20,000,000. One millimetre on that map is 20 km; the whole 6.77 x 14.62 km AOI is smaller than a single map unit. Drawing it as a layer would imply geological detail the product cannot support. It is cited as regional context instead. Searched USGS Astrogeology for a higher-resolution map of the MSL site on 2026-11-14 and found none published as GIS data.

geochem.title: MRO CRISM map-projected targeted summary parameters (MTRDR)
geochem.discovery_note: A spatial ODE search needs ihid, iid and pt together; any one alone is ignored. Ten MTRDR observations intersect the AOI. ODE indexes each by its *_if*_mtr3 I/F cube, so the summary cube is found through the product's file listing, not by guessing a filename.
geochem.reference: Viviano-Beck et al. (2014), Revised CRISM spectral parameters and summary products, J. Geophys. Res. Planets 119, 1403-1431

scenes.note: Full-resolution targeted observation at 18 m/px. Covers the AOI across its full width but stops short at both ends in latitude, so it supplies most of the AOI and none of the extreme north or south.

Half-resolution long targeted observation at 36 m/px. Its footprint contains the whole AOI, so it fills what the FRT scene misses. Used only where the FRT scene has no valid value, and flagged per cell in coverage.png because it is half the resolution.

bands.name: BD530_2
bands.mineralogy: nanophase and crystalline iron oxide, hematite

bands.name: OLINDEX3
bands.mineralogy: olivine, unweathered mafic sand and bedrock

bands.name: BD1900R2
bands.mineralogy: hydrated phases of any kind, not diagnostic on its own

bands.name: BD2210_2
bands.mineralogy: opaline silica and Al-clay, the signature of altered volcanic ash (tuff)

bands.name: D2300
bands.mineralogy: Fe/Mg smectite, formed where water stood or flowed

bands.name: SINDEX2
bands.mineralogy: polyhydrated sulfate, precipitated as water evaporated

geochem.bands_note: Band order is read from the ENVI header at run time, never hard-coded: the header's `band names` list is the only authority for which of the 60 planes is which parameter, and both scenes were checked to carry the same order.
geochem.no_data: The sentinel is the ENVI header's `data ignore value` (65535.0). The PDS label carries no NULL keyword, so the header has to be read.
geochem.caveat: These are spectral indices, not mineral abundances. A high index means the shape the parameter measures is present in that pixel's spectrum; it is evidence for a mineral group, not a measurement of how much is there. Thin dust cover, slope and illumination all move these numbers.

unit_derivation.method: A cell joins a unit where a summary parameter exceeds that scene's own AOI background median by sigma_k robust standard deviations, and never below the credibility floor. Thresholds are computed per scene at build time, not stored here, because they depend on the scene statistics; the values actually used are written into public/data/geochem/units.json every build, along with three checks (cross-scene consistency, stratigraphic ordering, slope dependence).
unit_derivation.audit: These two numbers are the whole of the hand-chosen input. Change sigma_k to move every threshold together; the build reports what each became and fails if the two scenes start classifying at rates more than 10x apart.
unit_derivation.known_limitation: The derived units do NOT reproduce the published clay-below-sulfate ordering on Mount Sharp. That is measured and stated in units.json rather than hidden: the layer is for finding ground worth visiting, not for naming minerals.

science_regions.method: Region extents are to be built from Curiosity's own traverse: the sols the rover spent working each unit define a corridor on the ground. This is used in preference to tracing the annotated 'Proposed Path up Mount Sharp' figure, because that figure has no georeferencing control points published with it and tracing it by eye would produce boundaries we could not defend. The annotated map informs which sol ranges belong to which unit.

radiation.citation: Hassler, D. M. et al. (2014), Mars' Surface Radiation Environment Measured with the Mars Science Laboratory's Curiosity Rover, Science 343, 1244797
radiation.note: Baseline surface dose rate and the solar-particle-event scenario are modelled from published RAD results, not ingested telemetry. The SPE is explicitly labelled a scenario in the UI.

weather.basis: Curiosity REMS published seasonal values for Gale Crater
weather.note: Daily temperature, pressure and wind cycle modelled from published REMS ranges; dust opacity is a user-selectable scenario, not a measurement.

rejected._comment: Sources checked and NOT used, with the reason. Kept so the choice is auditable.

trek_gale_dem_tiles.reason: Trek serves this DEM as 8-bit greyscale PNG tiles: a whole z=14 tile contains only ~5 distinct grey levels, i.e. roughly 14 m of elevation per level once stretched over Gale's relief. Adequate as a picture, unusable for slope or hazard derivation. Replaced by the 32-bit float PDS DTM.

usgs_mola_463m.reason: Real and reachable (2.1 GB GeoTIFF) but 463 m/px gives ~15 x 32 pixels over this AOI. Too coarse for EVA routing.

usgs_hrsc_mola_blend_200m.reason: 404 - the filename guessed from memory does not exist. Not used.

murray_lab_ctx.reason: Host unreachable from the build environment at probe time.

nasa_worldview.reason: Earth observation data. Used only as design inspiration for the layer UX, credited on the About page. No Earth data is placed on the Mars map.

perseverance_raw_images.reason: Mars 2020 operates in Jezero Crater, not Gale. Listed on the About page as a related resource only.

crism_global_mineral_map.reason: The CRISM multispectral global mosaic is published at 256 pixels per degree, about 180 m/px. Over this 6.77 x 14.62 km AOI that is roughly 38 x 81 pixels, so a single pixel spans several science stations and no unit boundary inside the AOI would be real. Rejected for the same reason as the global geologic map: too coarse for the question the app asks. The targeted MTRDR cubes at 18 m/px were used instead.

crism_mtrdr_browse_images.reason: Every MTRDR observation ships ready-made BR* browse rasters, one per mineral theme, which would have been far less work to use. They are 8-bit renders with a per-scene contrast stretch already applied, so the pixel values are display levels, not index values: two scenes stretched differently cannot be compared or thresholded. The Trek DEM was rejected on exactly this ground, and being consistent matters more than the saved effort. The 32-bit float summary cube was used instead.

crism_if_cube.reason: The 1.1 GB I/F cube holds the full calibrated spectra and would allow our own spectral parameters. Computing them would mean reproducing the continuum removal and the atmospheric and photometric corrections already applied in the published summary cube, with no way to validate the result. Using the archive's own summary parameters keeps the numbers traceable to a published method.

usgs_gale_geologic_map.reason: Searched on 2026-11-14 for a published Gale Crater or Mount Sharp geologic map released as GIS data at AOI scale. The USGS catalogue has the 1:20,000,000 global map (see `geology`) and nothing finer for this site. Published MSL-site unit maps exist in the literature as figures without georeferencing control points, which is the same problem as the proposed-path figure in `science_regions`. So the geochemical units here are derived from CRISM indices rather than digitised from a published map, and are labelled DERIVED.
